## Overview

ELDERCARE-AF (ClinicalTrials.gov number NCT02801669) compared a once-daily 15-mg dose of [edoxaban](./edoxaban.md) with placebo in elderly Japanese patients aged 80 years or older with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation who were not considered appropriate candidates for oral anticoagulant therapy at doses approved for stroke prevention. The primary efficacy end point was the composite of stroke or systemic embolism and the primary safety end point was major bleeding according to the definition of the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis ([src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228.md)).

## Reported results

A total of 984 patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to edoxaban 15 mg daily (492 patients) or placebo (492 patients); 681 completed the trial and 303 discontinued. The annualized rate of stroke or systemic embolism was 2.3% with edoxaban and 6.7% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.34; 95% CI 0.19 to 0.61; P<0.001), while major bleeding occurred at 3.3% and 1.8% per year respectively (hazard ratio 1.87; 95% CI 0.90 to 3.89; P=0.09), with substantially more gastrointestinal bleeding events in the edoxaban group. Death from any cause did not differ substantially between groups (9.9% versus 10.2%) ([src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228.md)).

The trial was funded by Daiichi Sankyo ([src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228.md)).
